title: Trump Orders Withdrawal of 5,000 US Troops from Germany in Feud with Chancellor Merz
detail: The Pentagon announced the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 US service members from Germany — roughly one-seventh of the 36,000 stationed there — framed as retaliation after Chancellor Friedrich Merz publicly criticized US strategy in the Middle East conflict. Trump stated on May 2 that cuts would go 'a lot further than 5,000.' The move represents the most significant reduction in US military presence in Germany since the Cold War drawdown of the 1990s, with major implications for NATO cohesion and Germany's own defense posture. Germany's defense establishment warned the withdrawal would create critical capability gaps in the NATO eastern flank.

media.caption: Trump orders withdrawal of 5,000 US troops from Germany amid Merz-Trump feud over Middle East strategy

title: SPD Attacks CDU Welfare Cuts at May Day Rallies, Deepening Coalition Crisis
detail: SPD co-leader and Labour Minister Bärbel Bas used May Day rallies across Germany to denounce CDU-led coalition welfare cuts as 'despicable' and warned of a 'swansong for the German welfare state.' Chancellor Friedrich Merz responded sharply, demanding SPD ministers 'return to work emotionally' and focus on governing rather than campaign rhetoric. The public confrontation underscored the fundamental tensions within the CDU/CSU–SPD grand coalition, which a Japan Times analysis that week described as 'at war with itself.' Three quarters of German voters in the INSA poll told pollsters the coalition was failing.

media.caption: Germany's CDU-SPD coalition publicly clashes as SPD attacks welfare cuts at May Day rallies
